newsitem.title: USA: Merck Q3 sales cut by 2 pct points by forex.
newsitem.headline: Merck Q3 sales cut by 2 pct points by forex.

text.p: Merck and Co Inc, reporting higher third quarter results, said on Wednesday that its sales growth was reduced by two percentage points by foreign exchange flucuations.
It was the same impact reported for the second quarter.
The strong U.S. dollar has trimmed the value of U.S. multinationals' foreign sales in dollar terms.
Merck reported third quarter sales of $4.98 billion, up from $4.17 billion a year ago, a 19 percent rise.
It posted earnings per share of $0.83, up from $0.70 a year ago and beating the First Call consensus estimate of $0.81.

Adjusted for effects of the divestitures of Medco Behavioral Care Corp in the fourth quarter of 1995 and Kelco in the first quarter of 1995, Merck's sales for the 1996 third quarter and first nine months grew 22 percent, the company said.

"Income growth for the first nine months was driven by strong unit volume gains," said Merck Chief Executive Raymond Gilmartin. "The unfavorable effects of inflation, net of price, and exchange were partially offset by cost controls and productivity improvements in manufacturing and selling, general and administrative expenses."
The drug maker's nine-month net was $2.84 billion, a 15 percent rise over the year-ago period. Its nine-month earnings per share was $2.33, a 17 percent rise.
